title: Add remediation SLA timers + breach alerts (Slack + paging) keyed by severity/tier
author: Dylan Brooks
description: Context: As part of the Reliability Program (Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping), we’re adding enforcement around remediation expectations. This PR implements remediation SLA timers and breach alerting (Slack + paging) keyed by incident severity and customer tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). It ships with conservative defaults, is fully config-driven, and includes safeguards to avoid noisy paging. What’s in this PR: 1) SLA policy evaluation + due time computation: New module computes SLA due timestamps for (a) time-to-mitigate (TTM) and (b) time-to-fix (TTF) based on incident {severity, tier}. We derive start_time from the incident declared timestamp (incident-bot created_at / incident record start_at) and persist computed due_at values into the incident record. Timers are recomputed if severity or tier changes. 2) Breach notifications: Adds two notification thresholds: (a) “approaching breach” at 80% of remaining time (Slack only) and (b) “breach” at 100% (Slack + paging depending on policy). Paging is enabled only for Sev0/Sev1 for Dedicated/Private by default; Hosted Sev0 pages, Hosted Sev1/Sev2 are Slack-only by default. 3) Config defaults + overrides: Adds a versioned YAML config `configs/reliability/remediation_sla.yaml` with defaults for each tier and severity. Also supports per-incident overrides for: pause_reason (force majeure), customer_caused (does not stop timer, but annotates notifications), and suppression window (temporary; requires reason + actor). 4) Telemetry: Emits metrics for compliance reporting and alert tuning: `incident_sla_due_seconds{tier,severity,phase}` and `incident_sla_breach_total{tier,severity,phase,breach_type}` plus structured logs including incident_id, due_at, and whether paging was suppressed. Metrics label cardinality is bounded (tier/severity/phase enums only). 5) Runbook wiring: Adds runbook link in Slack breach message, and includes explicit “how to pause/override” guidance with audit trail requirements. Behavior details: - Timer start: when incident transitions into ACTIVE (declared), not when the first alert fired. - Timer stop: TTM stops when incident is marked MITIGATED; TTF stops when incident is marked RESOLVED. - Severity/tier changes: Recompute due_at from the original start_time for that phase; we also emit an audit log entry noting the policy change. - Pauses: Only supported for force majeure (e.g., cloud provider region outage) and requires `pause_reason` + `approved_by` on the incident record. Paused incidents still send a daily Slack reminder in #eng-sre to ensure they’re not forgotten. - Dual tracking: If Security Ops flags an incident as security-classified, this SLA evaluator continues to run for reliability severity/tier but adds `security_flag=true` to logs and includes a handoff note in notifications. Slack message format (breach): `:rotating_light: Remediation SLA BREACH (TTM) - Sev1 Dedicated` + incident link + owner + due_at + time_over + action buttons (ack, page owner, pause with reason). Pager payload includes incident_id, tier, severity, phase (TTM/TTF), and owner team. Why this approach: - Config-driven to align with evolving customer commitments without code changes. - Low-cardinality telemetry for dashboards and long-term reporting. - Conservative paging defaults to avoid alert fatigue while still making breaches visible and measurable. Follow-ups (out of scope here): - Hooking taxonomy incident_type into SLA policy (phase 2); today it’s keyed only by tier/severity. - Console surfacing for CS/ops (tracked separately). - Backfill for historical incidents (ENG-4827). Testing: - Unit tests for policy evaluator (matrix coverage). - Integration tests for Slack notification payloads and PagerDuty routing suppression logic. - “Time travel” tests using fake clock to validate approaching-breach and breach scheduling. Risk/rollout: - Feature flags: `remediation_sla.enabled` and `remediation_sla.paging_enabled`. - Default rollout plan: enable Slack-only for all tiers for 1 week; enable paging for Dedicated/Private Sev0/Sev1 after tuning. - Includes a kill switch to disable all SLA notifications if noise is higher than expected.
commits: sre/incident-sla: add remediation SLA policy evaluator + due time computation
control-plane/incidents: persist due_at + pause metadata; add audit log entries for policy changes
alerts: add Slack notifier for approaching-breach + breach events
pager: add breach paging routing (guarded by config + tier/severity gates)
tests: fake clock integration tests for scheduler + notification thresholds
docs: add runbook link + pause/override guidance in breach message template
changed_areas: docs/oncall (runbook snippet referenced in Slack alerts)
notable_snippets: configs/reliability/remediation_sla.yaml (new): tiers: hosted/dedicated/private; severities: sev0/sev1/sev2; phases: ttm/ttf; defaults include paging gates and 80% warning threshold
services/reliability/sla/policy.ts (new): computeDueAt(startAt, tier, severity, phase) with enum validation and audit logging on recompute
services/alerts/slack/templates/remediation_sla_breach.ts (new): standardized breach message with owner, due_at, time_over, runbook link, and pause/ack buttons
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes: We need to be explicit about the start/stop semantics (ACTIVE->MITIGATED/RESOLVED) and make sure severity changes don’t reset the clock in a way that hides breaches. Also add guidance for when to use pause vs suppression.

Dylan Brooks (author): Updated description + added audit log entry on any recompute; clock is anchored to phase start_time. Added `pause_reason` requirements and a daily reminder for paused incidents.

Allison Grant: Metrics look fine; please confirm labels are bounded enums only (no incident_type, no owner labels). Also please add a single counter for breaches rather than emitting a per-incident gauge that could churn.

Dylan Brooks (author): Confirmed: labels are tier/severity/phase/breach_type only. Switched breach reporting to `incident_sla_breach_total` counter and kept due time as a value emitted on incident state change (not continuously).
Aisha Bello: Can we emit “approaching breach” as a distinct event for dashboards? Also, do we have a knob to disable paging entirely while we tune?

Dylan Brooks (author): Added `incident_sla_warning_total{...}` counter for 80% warnings and feature flag `remediation_sla.paging_enabled` default false. Slack-only remains enabled behind `remediation_sla.enabled`.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated expectations: paging for Sev1 Dedicated is OK, but we need a carve-out for large cloud-provider incidents (force majeure). Make sure the pause path is auditable and doesn’t silently stop all notifications.

Dylan Brooks (author): Implemented pause with required `pause_reason` + `approved_by` and continued daily Slack reminder in #eng-sre while paused; breach paging is suppressed while paused but the incident record retains due_at and pause metadata.
Ethan Park: Any schema changes to incident records must include migration notes. Also, ensure pause/suppression changes are recorded in the control plane audit log.

Dylan Brooks (author): Added migration for new fields (due_at_ttm, due_at_ttf, pause_reason, pause_approved_by, suppression_until) and added audit log events `incident.sla_policy_recomputed` and `incident.sla_pause_updated`.
Nikhil Sharma: Hosted tier shouldn’t page for Sev1 by default; Slack is fine. Please double-check defaults match that and link the runbook for overrides.
Dylan Brooks (author): Defaults updated: Hosted pages only on Sev0. Added runbook link and quick steps for override/pause in Slack message.
Rafael Mendes: Approving contingent on rollout plan being documented in the PR and feature flags defaulting to safe values.
Dylan Brooks (author): Rollout plan added; paging flag defaults false. Thanks.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Rafael Mendes into main
release_notes: Internal: remediation SLA timers + breach notifications are now available behind `remediation_sla.enabled` / `remediation_sla.paging_enabled`. Default config is Slack-only; paging disabled by default.
